thread:
maria: Hey team — started getting a spike of DNS resolution failures from edge-gpu nodes in apac around 03:10 UTC. ~15-25% of modelfetch calls are ENOTFOUND. Not seeing obvious packet drops on LB.
josh: ugh. any pattern? same pod/node? trace route? region-only? :thinking:
maria: looks cluster-wide in the apac pool. Node-level logs show lots of `getaddrinfo` failing then succeeding on retry. TTLs on queries look normal. No deploys at the time.
kai: can you paste the resolv.conf from an affected node?
maria: sure — snippet below:
```
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 100.64.0.10
options ndots:5 timeout:1 attempts:2 rotate
```
josh: rotate + ndots:5 + short timeout — that combination can expose upstream jitter. If upstream / stub forwarder flaps, some queries timeout quickly and the client gives up.
infra-bot: deploy-monitor: no active infra deploys in apac between 03:00-03:30 UTC
maria: also noticed iptables conntrack counters incrementing for established NAT entries then sudden resets on some nodes.
kai: do we have any NAT/egress flapping in the edge-nat pool? maybe conntrack table getting pruned due to pressure.
josh: checking metrics... apac-nat-1 conntrack usage spiked before the DNS errors. Might be a NAT gateway auto-restart (kube-proxy or NAT gateway) causing short egress path resets.
maria: hypothesis: resolver requests hit an upstream forwarder that intermittently rejects UDP (ICMP/port-unreachable) and with ndots:5 clients try domain search first which adds extra lookups. Short timeout means more ENOTFOUND observed.
kai: two mitigation paths: increase timeout/attempts via DHCP/resolvconf for cluster until we stabilize, or add a local stub resolver (systemd-resolved / node-local) to absorb upstream jitter.
josh: can we test node-local-dns on a small canary? also we should try lowering ndots to 1 for modelfetch-heavy nodes so they don't do search-suffix retries.
maria: trying a quick test — on one node updated resolv.conf to `options ndots:1 timeout:2 attempts:2` and launched a small loop of modelfetchs for 10m.
infra-bot: telemetry: apac test node modelfetch success rate jumped from 78% -> 99% after ndots change
kai: nice. that suggests search-suffix retries were amplifying the effect of upstream timeouts.
josh: we should still root-cause NAT restarts. I'll check control-plane logs for kube-proxy and our cloud NAT for restarts around 03:05-03:15 UTC.
maria: opened a short-lived mitigation PR to roll ndots/timeouts for apac edge pool and to toggle node-local-dns canary. Will link in #eng-releases once ready.
kai: long-term let's deploy a small UDP-forwarder with retry logic and switch modelfetch to prefer A/AAAA direct queries when possible. Also add conntrack pressure alerts.
josh: +1. Thx for the rapid triage, @maria. If NAT restart root cause is infra, we'll escalate to network-ops.
maria: passing to net-ops if we confirm cloud nat flapping. For now canary NDOTS change seems low risk. :thumbsup:
